front.zh: 現代俳句 & 變奏   系列《 2 》

en: Heaven and earth possess great beauty yet say nothing
The color of the grass reflects the slanting light
The dragonfly floats upon the water

points.zh:
「天地有大美而不言，四時有明法而不議，萬物有成理而不說。」
--莊子《知北遊 》
「天何言哉，四時行焉，百物生焉，天何言哉。」
--孔子。《論語。陽貨篇》

en: Leave myself in the depths of night
Keeping hold of a stretch of quiet
Watching the mortal world recede like a passing traveler

zh: 把風乾的少年往事加醬
en: Season the wind-dried memories of youth
A summer afternoon
Drinking wine together with friends
There is always a journey
Light shines faintly through the thick fog
Blurred, romantic

zh: 滿山滿谷，吉野櫻，四重樱 ----
齊柏林翻轉鏡頭 :  鄉愁逼近
en: Filling every mountain and valley, Yoshino cherry, Shizhong cherry ----
Yushan junipers, gnarled and coiling, gaze toward the clouded sky
Chi Po-lin turns his lens: homesickness draws near

points.zh:
吉野櫻，四重櫻 ，是阿里山盛開的櫻花。
玉山圓柏屬於柏科植物，可能是台灣最古老的植物，比檜木還久遠。直徑1公尺的樹體，年齡至少有2000年。多數生長於海拔3400公尺以上的高山，如玉山，雪山，馬博拉斯山等。玉山圓柏最引人注目的特徵是極端的體形變異，在雪線邊缘避風處爲高拔俊挺的喬木，在雪線之上則是低矮匍匐的灌木。大多數生長於山巔絶嶺的艱困惡地，復因風暴，霜急雪覆，低温乾旱，土質貧瘠等環境壓力的折磨，終而雕鑿出盤虬曲張的枝幹，緊伏地表而匍匐綿亙，形成所謂的「矮盤灌叢」。有如大自然雕塑的盆景。糾纏絞結的變體軀幹，充滿頑强抗争的無比氣勢，在台灣高山絕地，迸發無窮的生命張力和韌力，望之令人震憾感動。

en: At night, rowing a boat across the Milky Way
Scooping up the brightest star, Sirius
By the conscience of heaven and earth

points.zh: 德國哲學家康德說  :「天上有星星，地上有良心」。
points.en: The German philosopher Kant said: "Above there are stars in the sky; on earth there is conscience."

zh: 當悲多芬的月光曲響起
en: When Beethoven's Moonlight Sonata begins to play
I fall silent, wordless
That summer, with you
It is all trouble you have caused
Faster to turn hostile than to turn a page
Facebook, a face full of helplessness
The seasons shift and change
The journey arrives, just like that
Will we leave hand in hand?
Basho writes haiku in his banana-leaf hut
The wind blows along the Narrow Road to the Deep North
Greened the banana leaves

points.zh:
松尾芭蕉 (1644-1694) ，是低級武土的兒子，1664年出版第一部俳諧詩集，此後作品豊富，以俳句為主，他公認的功績是把俳句形式推向頂峰，有日本俳聖之譽。1682年開始使用芭蕉為俳號，隱居處為「芭蕉庵」。1689年，時年46歲，自東京出發，徒步穿越日本本州北部深奧內部，以半年時間行走2400公里，并以此行程所見所思所感寫下傳世之作「奧之細道」，內容以「寂」為主題概念，以及人對自然的歸屬感。
「奧之細道」位於日本本州東北，是有名的歷史古道，「奧」是道路深處之意，「細」爲細長之路。芭蕉行經之沿途，留有多處吟咏俳句石碑。
芭蕉深受莊子，陶淵明，李白，杜甫，王維等詩人的影響，其俳句內容包羅萬象，在在都有唐宋詩詞的內涵和韻味。諸如 :
1. 沉寂古池，青蛙跳入，撲通一聲響。
2. 萬籟閒寂，蟬鳴入岩石。
3. 年歲徒長，依然蓑衣與草鞋。
4. 水鳥嘴，沾有梅瓣白。
5. 東有新月，西有夕陽，一地菜花黃。
一片春愁待酒澆，
江上舟搖，樓上帘招。
秋娘渡與泰娘橋，
風又飄飄，雨又蕭蕭。
何日歸家洗客袍，
銀字笙調，心字香燒。
流光容易把人拋，
紅了櫻桃，綠了芭蕉。
--南宋。蔣捷《一剪梅》
points.en:
Matsuo Basho (1644–1694) was the son of a low-ranking samurai. In 1664 he published his first collection of haikai poetry, and thereafter produced abundant work, primarily haiku; his widely recognized achievement was to bring the haiku form to its peak, earning him the title of Japan's Haiku Sage. In 1682 he began using "Basho" as his poetic name, and his hermitage was called the "Basho Hut." In 1689, at the age of 46, he set out from Edo (Tokyo) and traveled on foot through the deep interior of northern Honshu, covering 2,400 kilometers over half a year, and from what he saw, thought, and felt on this journey he wrote his enduring masterpiece 'Narrow Road to the Deep North' (Oku no Hosomichi), whose central theme is "sabi" (quiet solitude) and the sense of belonging between humans and nature.
The 'Narrow Road to the Deep North' lies in northeastern Honshu, Japan, and is a famous historic path; "oku" means the depths of the road, and "hoso" means a narrow, long path. Along the route Basho traveled, many stone monuments inscribed with his haiku remain.
Basho was deeply influenced by Zhuangzi, Tao Yuanming, Li Bai, Du Fu, Wang Wei, and other poets; his haiku encompass all things, and everywhere carry the essence and flavor of Tang and Song poetry. For example:
1. Into the tranquil old pond, a frog leaps in, a splash resounds.
2. In the utter stillness, a cicada's cry seeps into the rock.
3. Another year has passed in vain, still the same straw raincoat and sandals.
4. On the water bird's beak, a trace of white plum petal clings.
5. New moon in the east, setting sun in the west, a field of yellow rapeseed flowers.
A whole spring's sorrow waits to be washed away with wine,
a boat rocks on the river, a tavern banner beckons from above.
At Qiuniang's ferry and Tainiang's bridge,
the wind drifts on and on, the rain falls soft and thin.
When shall I return home to wash my traveler's robe,
to tune the silver-inlaid reed pipe, to burn incense shaped like the character "heart"?
The swift light of time so easily casts a person aside —
the cherries have reddened, the banana leaves have greened.
-- Southern Song. Jiang Jie, 'A Sprig of Plum Blossom'
